title: faderz WebSocket server message
description: Messages a replica sends on /api/v1/ws. replica names the sending replica. Every message is a JSON text message defined here, except meter frames, which are binary messages laid out as in $defs/MeterFrame. hello is answered with replicas, then snapshot or resume; deltas follow in revision order. A client that sees a revision other than its own plus one sends resync. The replica sends ping every 250 ms and answers every client ping with pong (heartbeat rules: client-message.schema.json#/$defs/Ping). Meter frames and control requests go to primary connections only. Counters, selections and presence go to every connection; presence lists the sessions connected to the sending replica only. Meter frames are paced by the client's credits and dropped, never queued, while the connection holds none; deltas are never dropped: a client whose queue fills with deltas gets a snapshot instead.

Snapshot.description: Full replicated state at a global revision. The layout of the meter frames on this connection follows shape ($defs/MeterFrame).

you.description: The owner record of this connection.

epoch.description: Epoch of revision. A client holding state of another epoch learns from it that the cluster was restored or started empty: that state is not in the cluster history.

stale.description: The replica could not confirm that this state is the cluster's latest (client-message.schema.json, read index): it is cut off from the quorum or could not catch up within 2 s. revision may be older than the lastRevision of the hello or resync.

Resume.description: Answer to hello or resync with lastRevision: every delta after lastRevision, in order. revision is the global revision after the last of them.

you.description: The owner record of this connection.

epoch.description: Epoch of revision, the one the hello or resync carried: a resume never crosses epochs.

stale.description: The replica could not confirm that this state is the cluster's latest (client-message.schema.json, read index): it is cut off from the quorum or could not catch up within 2 s. revision may be older than the lastRevision of the hello or resync.

Ahead.description: Answers a hello or resync whose epoch is the cluster epoch and whose lastRevision is above the highest revision the cluster has committed in it, in place of holding it: the client holds state the cluster does not have. A restore from a backup or an empty start gives the cluster a new epoch, so a client of the earlier history is answered with a snapshot of the new epoch instead. The replica holds nothing for the connection. A client takes the cluster state with a resync without lastRevision, which the replica answers with a snapshot at revision.

epoch.description: The cluster epoch, the one the hello or resync carried.

revision.description: Highest revision the cluster has committed.

lastRevision.description: The lastRevision of the hello or resync.

Delta.description: One entry of the replicated log at global revision `revision`. The server batches the commands that arrive within one processing block into one entry, so a delta may carry changes from several origins; when two commands in it write the same control, the later one wins and only its value is listed. atIndex is the sample index at which the parameter changes take effect on every replica; absent when only ownership changed. A delta carries neither changes nor owners when its entry changed nothing a client shows: a control request, which only its holder's connection receives, as a controlRequest message. origins lists every client command applied in it; absent for server-side changes (tally, console status, lease expiry, REST writes).

Ack.description: A command that changed nothing. duplicate: its id was already applied (revision is the one it was applied at); stale: its seq is not above the last one applied from its session for the same control (client-message.schema.json#/$defs/Set); noop: the state already held the value or ownership.

Replicas.description: Replica set as seen by the sending replica, with health and whether each can commit, and what the sending replica was built from. Sent after hello and whenever a role, health or quorum changes.

MeterFrame.description:
Binary WebSocket message with one meter frame of the sending replica; every other server message is a JSON text message. Sent on primary connections only, at most once per meter period of the replica (40 ms, 25 per second), and only while the connection holds a credit (client-message.schema.json#/$defs/Credit). All integers are little endian.
Header: byte 0 magic 0x4D (ASCII M); byte 1 format version, 4; byte 2 length L of the replica id, 1 to 32; byte 3 reserved, 0; bytes 4 to 7 sequence, uint32; bytes 8 to 11 layout fingerprint, uint32; from byte 12, the L bytes of the replica id (ReplicaRef id) in ASCII; then one zero byte when L is odd. The values start at offset H = 12 + L + (L mod 2) and run to the end of the message, as int16.
sequence counts the meter periods of the replica, one per period whether or not this connection is sent a frame, and wraps from 4294967295 to 0. The difference between two received sequences minus one is the number of frames this connection was not sent.
Layout: the frame carries no shape and no ids. For each channel of shape.channels in order: peak legs, truePeak legs, then momentary. Then for each element of shape.buses, then of shape.auxes, then of shape.mixMinus, each in order: peak legs, truePeak legs, rms legs, loudness momentary, shortTerm, integrated, lra, maxMomentary, maxShortTerm, then correlation, then flags. Then for each element of shape.monitorOutputs in order: peak legs. Then for each element of shape.ducks in order: key, envelope, then duck flags. An element has width legs, in layout order. flags bit 0 is loudness integratedValid, bit 1 loudness lraStable; the other bits are 0. A duck group's key is the largest level of its keys after their key filters and key gains over the last 10 ms the engine computed it in, in centi-dBFS, -32768 while the group is not in use; envelope is how far the group ducks its targets, 0 to 10000 for 0 to 1, a target lowered by its depth times envelope / 10000 dB, 0 while not in use; duck flags bit 0 is engaged, the detector triggered or holding; the other bits are 0. A frame holds the sum of 2 * width + 1 over the channels plus the sum of 3 * width + 8 over the buses, auxes and mix-minus outputs plus the sum of width over the monitor outputs plus 3 per duck group values.
Values: centi-units, that is dBFS, dBTP, LUFS, LU or correlation times 100: v = floor(x * 100 + 0.5) in IEEE 754 double arithmetic, clamped to -32767..32767. A leg of digital silence, -Infinity, is -12000, the floor of a leg. -32768 stands for null, a loudness or correlation of -Infinity, or no measurement.
Decoding into model.schema.json objects: a value v other than -32768 gives v / 100 clamped to the range of its field: -120..30 for legs (MeterDb) and for the loudness values, 0..100 for lra, -1..1 for correlation. -32768 gives -120 for a leg (MeterDb has no null) and null for a loudness value or correlation. A channel gives ChannelMeter {peak, truePeak, momentary}; a bus, aux or mix-minus output gives BusMeter {peak, truePeak, rms, loudness, correlation}. A monitor output gives MonitorMeter {peak}. A duck group gives DuckMeter {key, envelope, engaged}: key null for -32768, else v / 100 clamped to -120..30; envelope v / 10000 clamped to 0..1; engaged from bit 0. They validate against model.schema.json#/$defs/ChannelMeter, #/$defs/BusMeter, #/$defs/MonitorMeter and #/$defs/DuckMeter.
Fingerprint: FNV-1a 32-bit (offset basis 2166136261, prime 16777619) over the ASCII text that holds, for each element in layout order, section/id/width; where section is c for a channel, b for a bus, a for an aux, m for a mix-minus output, o for a monitor output and d for a duck group, whose width is 1, for example c/ch1/1;b/pgm/2;d/comm/1; .
Shape changes: the layout is a function of the shape the client got in its last snapshot. The shape is fixed while a server runs, so it changes only across a restart, and a replica restarted with another shape sends frames with another fingerprint. A decoder drops a frame whose magic, version, fingerprint or length (H + 2 * the value count of its layout) does not match its layout. On a fingerprint mismatch the client sends resync with full, its lastRevision and its epoch; the snapshot answering it carries the current shape, at a revision not older than the client's, and the frames after it follow that shape.
The example is the frame of replica rep at sequence 258 for a shape of channel ch1 (width 1) and bus pgm (width 2), with ch1 peak -6.5, truePeak -5.9 and momentary -20; pgm peak 0 and 3.21, truePeak 0.5 and -Infinity, rms -18 and -18.5, momentary -23, shortTerm null, integrated -23.46, lra 7.25, maxMomentary -21.5, maxShortTerm null, correlation 0.85, integratedValid true and lraStable false, and duck group comm with key -20, envelope 0.5 and engaged, in hexadecimal.

Counters.description: Engine counters of the sending replica, on every connection, standby ones included: after the snapshot or resume that answers its hello, and once per second. A replica that runs no engine sends none. A client takes them from its primary connection only; a standby connection receives them so a promoted standby has them at once.

Selections.description: What every session has selected (client-message.schema.json#/$defs/Select), on every connection, standby ones included: after the snapshot or resume that answers its hello, and whenever a selection changes or lapses with its session's lease. At most one such message per connection every 100 ms; changes within that time go out together in the next one. Lists every session with a selection, the receiving one included, at most one entry per session. Selections are not part of the replicated state, and a client takes them from its primary connection only; a standby connection receives them so a promoted standby has them at once.

session.description: The session, as its owner record: principal, handle, kind and the connection the message came through.

Presence.description: The sessions connected to this replica: every session with a WebSocket connection open on the replica that sent this message and that has sent a hello, its primary and standby connections counted once, the receiving one included, in the order they connected. Sent on every connection, standby ones included: after the snapshot or resume that answers its hello, and whenever a session connects, closes its last connection to this replica, sends another kind in a hello, or is active in another second. At most one such message per connection every 100 ms; changes within that time go out together in the next one. Presence is not part of the replicated state and is not shared between replicas: each replica lists only the sessions connected to it, so a client takes it from its primary connection only.

handle.description: The session's handle, as in its owner records (model.schema.json#/$defs/Owner).

kind.description: The kind its latest hello named.

user.description: Who the session is signed in as, for display: the display name the authentication gives (in oidc mode the provider's preferred_username, else its name claim; in proxy mode the user the proxy names), else token in token mode and anonymous otherwise. Never an email address or a subject id.

since.description: When the session's first connection open on this replica opened.

active.description: When the session last sent a command, a selection or a control request, to the second; since until then.

ControlRequest.description: Another session asks this one to give up a control it owns (client-message.schema.json#/$defs/Request). Sent to the primary connections of the owning session only. It changes nothing: the owner decides, and its ownership lapses with its lease in any case.

Error.description: A client message was refused. commandId names the refused command. For code 409 (control owned by another session) current and owner carry the control's current value and owner. Code 503 means not applied when answered: the replica could not commit the command, for example while it had no leader or quorum, or did not see it commit within its write timeout, in which case it may still be applied later, at most once. The client sends the command again with the same id and seq until it is answered otherwise or expires; a command applied late reaches every client as a delta like any other (client-message.schema.json). An error without commandId refuses a message that is not a command, such as a console registration (client-message.schema.json#/$defs/Console); code 429 refuses one beyond its rate limit.

Ping.description: Heartbeat, every 250 ms on every connection after hello. t is the replica's clock in milliseconds, echoed by pong; ping carries no state. Rules for both sides: client-message.schema.json#/$defs/Ping.

Pong.description: Answer to a client ping, echoing its t. Carries no state.
